title: Segmented edge audit pipeline and mTLS playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook captures an implementation pattern for segmented-edge private deployments where we combine RBAC v2 signals, a compact audit schema, and automated evidence packaging for SIEM export. Focus areas: VPC segmentation patterns for customer private deployments, host/gateway mTLS flows, firewall ruleset recommendations for minimal blast radius, and an evidence automation pipeline that produces tamper-evident artifacts for compliance reviews.

Context and goals
- Audience: SREs, infra engineers deploying customer Private, security reviewers, and internal compliance auditors.
- Goal: give a single-runbook that can be adapted to each customer’s topology and that outputs a predictable evidence bundle (logs + signed artifacts) suitable for SIEM ingestion and internal attestations.
- Constraints: must not assume cloud-provider-specific managed services (works on GCP/AWS/Azure), must support air-gapped/on-prem variants with the same schema.

High-level architecture (text diagram)
Customer VPC / On-prem network
  [Edge Gateway (mTLS) ] -- private L3 -> [Segmentation Firewall / Transit] -- L3 -> [Control Plane Collector] -- HTTPS -> [Evidence Orchestrator] -> [SIEM / S3 archive]

Notes on components
- Edge Gateway: terminates customer TLS, enforces client cert pinning for inbound connections from customer mTLS agents. Acts as the first policy enforcement point.
- Segmentation Firewall/Transit: enforces security groups/ACLs between subnets (compute, data, control). Must support port-based allowlists and identity-based rules when available.
- Control Plane Collector: lightweight agent cluster that aggregates audit events, signs rollups, and forwards to the Evidence Orchestrator.
- Evidence Orchestrator: normalizes different audit sources (rbac events, network flows, host attestations) into a compact audit format and emits signed bundles for SIEM ingestion and long-term storage.

VPC segmentation pattern (recommended)
- Subnets:
  - edge-subnet: only inbound from customer CIDR and operator-management CIDR; hosts edge gateways
  - app-subnet: model inference workers, no public egress except to artifact storage endpoints
  - control-subnet: collectors, admin interfaces; strictly whitelisted management hosts only
  - data-subnet (optional): persistent stores, encrypted, accessible only from app-subnet via service account rules
- Routing: use explicit route tables per-subnet; deny route propagation for edge-subnet to reduce lateral movement risk.
- Egress: block 0.0.0.0/0 egress from app-subnet and instead require NAT/proxy in control-subnet for approved destinations.

mTLS best-practices and flow
- Short-lived client certs (1h–24h) minted by customer or Redwood CA depending on deployment mode. Support JWKS-based rotation for gateway control plane.
- Mutual TLS at the following trust boundaries:
  - Customer agents -> Edge Gateway
  - Edge Gateway -> Control Plane Collector (mutual)
  - Collector -> Evidence Orchestrator (mTLS or signed JWTs)
- Keystore rotation: automated weekly rotation for ephemeral keys; monthly rotation for CA intermediate. Keep a rolling window of previous certs for 7 days for continuity in audits.
- Pinning & validation: gateways MUST validate CRL/OCSP or use certificate transparency checks (if available). For air-gapped, include an internal revocation endpoint mirrored from control-plane snapshots.

Firewall rules (examples, adapt to cloud provider syntax)
- edge-subnet -> control-subnet: allow TCP 443 (mTLS), src edge-subnet only
- edge-subnet -> app-subnet: deny direct; only allow through reverse-proxy or internal LB on specified ports (e.g., 8080, 8443)
- app-subnet -> data-subnet: allow TCP 5432 (db), 9200 (search) but restrict by service account tags
- control-subnet -> SIEM endpoint: allow 443 outbound to SIEM collector IP ranges
- management CIDR -> control-subnet: allow SSH/SSH bastion and HTTPS (admin) from operator IPs only

RBAC v2: practical mapping for segmented edge
- Policy model: role binding of (principal type: machine/service, resource, action). Example canonical binding:
  - role: inference.runner
  - principal: svc:customer-inference-agent@customerA
  - resources: model.deployments/*
  - actions: create.invoke, read.log
- Recommended minimal roles for components:
  - edge: edge.gateway.admin (deploy/configure), edge.gateway.proxy (forward)
  - collector: collector.ingest (write events), collector.admin
  - orchestrator: evidence.signer (sign bundles), evidence.writer (upload)
- Decision log: capture each RBAC decision as an audit event with trace_id and policy_version. Keep policy_version in the event to allow later repro.

Compact audit schema (example ACF - audit compact format)
- Fields (tab-delimited in text export or JSONL per line):
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - trace_id (uuid)
  - principal (string, e.g., svc:edge-gw-1)
  - principal_type (machine/user/service)
  - action (string: rb.Act or net.connect)
  - resource (string)
  - decision (allow/deny)
  - policy_version (semver)
  - src_ip
  - dst_ip
  - flow_label (string: segmentation label e.g., "app-1->db-1")
  - evidence_hash (sha256 hex)  // pointer to signed artifact entry
  - signature (base64) // optional for already-signed lines
- Example line (JSONL):
  {"timestamp":"2025-01-15T14:22:03Z","trace_id":"f2b3c1aa-...","principal":"svc:edge-gw-1","principal_type":"machine","action":"net.accept","resource":"edge:listener:443","decision":"allow","policy_version":"v2.1.0","src_ip":"203.0.113.45","dst_ip":"10.0.2.12","flow_label":"customerA-edge->collector","evidence_hash":"9f2e...","signature":"MEUCIQ..."}

Evidence automation pipeline (recommended steps)
1) Collect: Agents on gateways and hosts push compact events to local collector over mTLS.
2) Normalize: Collector maps provider-specific fields into ACF (audit compact format). Apply flow_label heuristics for segmentation context.
3) Batch & sign: Collector bundles events into time-windowed rollups (default 5m), canonicalizes ordering, computes SHA256 tree-of-files, signs root with evidence_signer identity.
4) Store & forward: Upload signed bundle to customer-owned artifact store (S3-compatible) plus push a copy to the centralized SIEM ingest endpoint.
5) Verify: Orchestrator posts verification events back into ACF with signed verification_entry referencing bundle hash and collector identity.

SIEM export mapping notes
- Export must preserve the evidence_hash field and the bundle manifest URL. SIEM parsers should treat signed bundles as primary evidence and keep signature metadata.
- Recommended field mapping for SIEM ingestion: timestamp, trace_id, principal, action, decision, flow_label, evidence_hash, bundle_url, signature, policy_version.
- For high-volume customers use a compressed JSONL + index approach (manifest + .jl.gz + .idx) where idx maps line offsets for fast lookup.

Operational playbook: hardening checklist (quick)
- [ ] Edge gateways run immutable images, no shell access; admin actions via ephemeral bastion with MFA.
- [ ] mTLS enabled for all inter-component traffic; no plaintext fallback.
- [ ] Keystores rotated according to policy; previous CA artifacts retained for 7 days.
- [ ] Firewall rules reviewed monthly and stored in IaC repo with PR audits.
- [ ] RBAC changes gated: PR -> policy test harness -> canary -> rollout. Store policy_version in each event.
- [ ] Evidence bundles auto-upload to customer archive and redundant central archive; retention policy declared in contract.
- [ ] SIEM parsers configured to validate signature of evidence bundles and raise alerts on verification failures.

Troubleshooting notes and gotchas
- When customers use overlapping CIDRs, prefer identity-based allowlists (service tags) rather than IP-only rules.
- In air-gapped installs, maintain a signed revocation list snapshot that collectors can reference; document the process to update snapshots.
- Watch clock drift across gateways/collectors; signed bundles require synchronized time (NTP or hardware RTC).

Open questions (for design review)
- Should signed evidence bundles be customer-signed as well (double attestation) or only Redwood-signed? Pros/cons in doc body.
- Do we adopt an ACF standard across all products or allow product-specific extensions? Recommend core required fields and freeform extension field.

Appendix: sample RBAC v2 policy JSON (minimal)
{
  "version":"v2.0",
  "bindings":[
    {"role":"edge.gateway.proxy", "principal":"svc:edge-gw-*","resources":["edge:listener:*"],"actions":["net.accept","net.connect"]}
  ]
}

Appendix: quick-start checklist for a new customer deployment (1–2 day ops runbook)
- Day 0: confirm network CIDRs and management CIDR; provision edge-subnet and control-subnet.
- Day 1: deploy Edge Gateway with mTLS (test with a short-lived client cert); deploy collector; run sample traffic.
- Day 2: enable evidence pipeline, produce initial signed bundle, verify SIEM ingest.

If this runbook is useful, next steps: convert the ACF schema above into a concise machine-readable JSON Schema and add a reference implementation to the private-deployments repo for the collector normalizer.

Comments / notes to reviewers
- Prioritize feedback on retention window (currently propose 1 year default for evidence bundles) and signature key management for on-prem customers.
- I purposely kept the audit schema compact to reduce bandwidth for offline environments; we can expand with optional extension fields if customers require.
